title: Balance the signal, not just the request count
description: Change workload shape, algorithm, failure domain, health policy, retries, and connection reuse. The model recomputes target pressure, retry amplification, handshake rate, and the user-visible serving result.

workloads.label: Uniform short requests
workloads.detail: Requests have similar cost and finish quickly, so request count is a reasonable load estimate.

workloads.label: Variable request cost
workloads.detail: Some requests hold backend work much longer; active requests reveal pressure better than arrival count.

workloads.label: Hot tenant with affinity
workloads.detail: One tenant owns 65% of traffic, so deterministic placement improves locality but concentrates load.

topologies.label: Four targets in one zone
topologies.detail: Instance failures have spare capacity, but one zonal event removes the whole serving pool.

topologies.label: Two targets in each of two zones
topologies.detail: The pool can route around one zone when the surviving zone has enough reserved capacity.

algorithms.label: Round robin
algorithms.detail: Even request counts; simple and predictable when targets and request cost are truly similar.

algorithms.label: Least active requests
algorithms.detail: Uses outstanding L7 work as a feedback signal and steers away from a target that stays busy.

algorithms.label: Consistent hash affinity
algorithms.detail: Keeps a key on a stable target for locality, but a hot key can dominate one target.

incidents.label: All targets healthy
incidents.detail: Every target is ready and has its full measured capacity.

incidents.label: app-a2 is alive but not ready
incidents.detail: The process accepts connections while caches and required dependencies are still warming.

incidents.label: app-a2 becomes a slow outlier
incidents.detail: The target passes active checks but live requests are slow and frequently fail.

incidents.label: zone-a stops serving
incidents.detail: Power, networking, or a shared zonal dependency removes every target in the entry zone.

retryPolicies.label: No proxy retry
retryPolicies.detail: Return the first result and let the caller follow the application contract.

retryPolicies.label: One budgeted, idempotent retry
retryPolicies.detail: Retry only declared-safe operations, capped at 10% of original traffic and inside the caller deadline.

retryPolicies.label: Two blind retries
retryPolicies.detail: Retry every failure twice without an idempotency contract or shared retry budget.
